newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end weaker on late fund sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end weaker on late fund sell-off.

text.p: Late fund selling erased gains in soybeans on Tuesday, following technical weakness in corn, with forecasts for rain in Brazil compounding losses, traders said.

Technically, the market weakened after it was unable to sustain gains above $7.50 per bushel and failed to break the near-term high at $7.54, technical traders said. Fund and local selling appeared after noon.
"They can't take out fifty-four ($7.54 in the March). Fifty-four is resistance plus there is rain in the forecast for later this week," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Forecasts called for rain to hit dry pockets of Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul on Thursday. The moisture should help ease concerns of drought-related crop losses.
"It's isolated spots," said Eloi Hilgert at the Rio Grande do Sul agricultural secretariat, referring to the dryness. "There's no indication of any crop loss yet."
Funds were buyers early. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought six million May. Refco Inc bought two million May and one million March and Merrill Lynch and ING each bought two million March.
Soybeans closed 5-1/4 to two cents per bushel lower with March down 5-1/4 at $7.44-1/2 a bushel.
In late dealings, Lee B. Stern, Refco Inc and Rosenthal Collins each sold 500,000 bushels March, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold three million May and one million March on the day and Griffin Trading spread two million March/May.
Volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts against Monday's actual volume of 41,694 contracts, according to CBOT figures.
